issues.legal_issue: A claim for specific performance of the performable part of a contract may be added by amendment at the appellate stage when the seller’s inability to perform the whole contract is first disclosed at that stage.
material_facts: The buyer sued for specific performance of an agreement covering two parcels of land.
At the appellate stage, the seller stated for the first time that he had no title to one parcel and that its owner had refused to transfer it to him.
The buyer amended the plaint to relinquish the claim to that parcel and compensation, while agreeing to pay the full contract price.
The buyer’s right to seek specific performance existed when the suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The buyer could seek partial specific performance by amendment at the appellate stage; the contrary ruling that the claim had to be made when the suit was filed was erroneous.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal is a continuation of the suit, and the appellate court may consider a matter the trial court could have decided if the claimant possessed the relevant right when the suit was filed. Relief under the Specific Relief Act, 1963, including under Section 12(3), may be sought at an appellate stage. The Court agreed with Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar and A.L. Parthasarathi Mudaliar v. Venkata Kondiah Chettiar.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and appeal_pending and inability_first_disclosed_on_appeal and claimant_amends_to_relinquish_unperformable_part_and_compensation and claimant_agrees_to_required_consideration and right_existed_when_suit_filed

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A buyer brought a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.appeal_pending: The claim was before an appellate court hearing an appeal that continued the suit.
predicates.inability_first_disclosed_on_appeal: The seller first disclosed during the appeal that the seller could not perform part of the contract.
predicates.claimant_amends_to_relinquish_unperforma: The buyer amended the pleading to give up the claim to the unperformable part and compensation for its non-performance.
predicates.claimant_agrees_to_required_consideratio: The buyer agreed to pay the consideration required for performance of the remaining part.
predicates.right_existed_when_suit_filed: The buyer possessed the right to seek the relevant relief when the suit was filed.

issues.definition: When a buyer’s right existed at filing and the seller’s inability is first disclosed on appeal, an amendment relinquishing the unperformable part and compensation and agreeing to the required consideration may be permitted in the pending specific-performance suit.

issues.legal_issue: A buyer may obtain specific performance of the part of a contract the seller can perform when the seller is unable to perform the whole contract and the buyer satisfies the required consideration and relinquishment conditions.
material_facts: The agreement covered two parcels, but the seller was unable to transfer one of them because he had no title to it.
The buyer agreed to take the parcel the seller could transfer, deposited the full contract price, and relinquished any claim to the other parcel and to compensation.
The first appellate court granted specific performance for the parcel the seller could transfer.
issues.conclusion: The first appellate court was justified in granting specific performance of the performable part of the contract on these facts.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits specific performance of the part a defaulting party can perform if the other party satisfies the applicable consideration requirement and relinquishes claims to performance of the remaining part and compensation. For a part that admits of compensation, the consideration is the contract consideration reduced by that attributable to the part left unperformed; for a part that does not admit of compensation, the consideration for the whole contract is required. The relief is discretionary and is ordinarily granted if there is no delay, laches, or other disability affecting the claimant.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and seller_unable_to_perform_part and buyer_pays_required_consideration and buyer_relinquishes_remaining_performance_and_compensation and no_delay_laches_or_other_disability

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A buyer brought a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.seller_unable_to_perform_part: The seller was unable to perform part of the contract.
predicates.buyer_pays_required_consideration: The buyer paid or agreed to pay the consideration required for the part the seller could perform.
predicates.buyer_relinquishes_remaining_performance: The buyer gave up claims to performance of the remaining part and to compensation for its non-performance.
predicates.no_delay_laches_or_other_disability: The buyer was not affected by delay, laches, or another disability that would weigh against the discretionary relief.

issues.definition: When a seller cannot perform part of a contract, a buyer who pays the required consideration and relinquishes claims to the remaining performance and compensation will ordinarily receive specific performance of the performable part if no relevant disability exists.
